newsitem.title: USA: CBS making efforts to win ratings - report.
newsitem.headline: CBS making efforts to win ratings - report.

text.p: U.S. television network CBS Corp, a unit of Westinghouse Electric Corp, expects to raise enough money for a winning bid for the broadcast rights to professional football as part of its efforts to raise ratings, according to the weekly financial tabloid Barron's.
The tabloid said in its March 3 edition CBS expected to get cash from two recently acquired cable outlets to acquire the rights to show games of the National Football League.

The network recently announced plans to pay more than $1.6 billion in stock for Gaylord Entertainment Co's Nashville Network and Country Music television, which produce $30 million in cash flow ever year, it said.
"That mound of moolah raises CBS's ability to bid heavily when the rights to bradocast pro football come up for grabs later this year," it said.
The tabloid said CBS would likely get its affiliate stations to contribute money for the bidding, too.

In other efforts, CBS had installed new news managers in its three largest markets -- New York, Chicago and Los Angeles -- to improve ratings, it said. Most of the news programs at its local stations had been falling behind local competitors, it added.
The tabloid said the network also planned to get its radio stations to boost profits and revenues by taking advertising away from local newspapers.
When Westinghouse eventually splits into two companies, one of them, CBS, will control all of the radio and television operations.
On Friday, Westinghouse's stock closed at 17-1/4 near a year low of 15-3/8.
